__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The home box's Prometheus (see CONTEXT.md §2) — remote-write target for Tempo's metrics-generator and scrape target for the Go worker's OTLP metrics via otel-collector's :8889 prometheus exporter.

description: Job-pipeline health for crowdmon's v1 flywheel: queue depth, download/chunk/pre-label duration, dedup ratio, pre-label throughput, reclaim rate, and every way a job permanently fails. Business data (annotations, dataset counts, model versions) lives in D1 and is shown in /admin, not here — see CONTEXT.md §7's "Do not rebuild Grafana inside /admin."

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: D1 job-table rows by status and kind, from the Go worker's `queue.depth` OTel gauge (queue_depth{status,kind} in Prometheus). The worker reads /api/jobs/stats once per metrics export interval and republishes it here; an empty panel means the worker is not exporting, which is itself the signal. A bad value is `pending` climbing while `claimed` stays flat: work is arriving faster than the one worker claims it, or the worker is down. `claimed` climbing without `done`/`failed` following is a stuck lease — the reaper (5-minute cron, CONTEXT.md §Q14) should be pulling those back to `pending` within roughly 7 minutes; if `claimed` keeps growing past that, the reaper itself is the thing that's broken. Scoped to `exported_job="crowdmon-worker"` like every other panel here: this Prometheus is shared with unrelated projects (infra/grafana/README.md), and `queue_depth` is a generic enough name that leaving it unscoped is one collision away from plotting somebody else's queue. Note the label is `exported_job`, not `job` — Prometheus relabels the OTel resource attribute out of the way of its own scrape-target labels, and a naive `job="crowdmon-worker"` filter silently matches nothing.

panels.title: Chunk duration
panels.description: p50 and p95 wall time to extract and dedup one 60s chunk — phase two of CONTEXT.md §Q13's two-phase fan-out; phase one has its own panel beside this one, from the Go worker's chunk.duration histogram (chunk_duration_seconds_bucket). Percentiles rather than an average: M8's chunk-granularity design (CONTEXT.md §4) means most chunks are fast and a minority — a fast-motion scene, a contended box — run long, and an average would hide exactly the tail an operator needs to see. A bad value is p95 pulling away from p50: that is chunks intermittently stalling rather than the whole fleet slowing down together, which points at contention (the reaper competing with a live worker for the same box's 2 cores, per CONTEXT.md's "parallelism argument is weak" note) rather than a systemic regression.

panels.title: Download duration
panels.description:
p50 and p95 wall time for a whole `download` job — fetch, ffprobe and fan-out, phase one of CONTEXT.md §Q13's two-phase split, which that section itself sizes at the bulk of a video's 10-20 minutes of work.

Issue #46 asks for "job duration", and a chunk is only one of the two job kinds. This half has no OTel instrument behind it: the Go worker meters frames and chunks (telemetry/metrics.go) because those are the numbers M8 needed, and nothing counts a download. What it does have is a span — `job.download`, opened in pipeline.go — so the duration comes from Tempo's metrics-generator rather than from an instrument, exactly the way reclaim and failure rate do on the API side. Adding a histogram to the worker would have been the other option and buys nothing here: the span already exists, and a second source for the same number is a second thing that can disagree.

A bad value is p95 climbing while chunk duration holds steady — that is yt-dlp or the residential uplink degrading, not extraction. Both are wall time, so a p95 far above p50 on a single-worker box usually means one long video rather than a slow one.

panels.title: Dedup ratio
panels.description:
Fraction of decoded frames *dropped* as near-duplicates by pHash dedup, computed as 1 - rate(frames_kept_total)/rate(frames_extracted_total).

Dropped rather than kept, though kept is the simpler query, because `frames.dedup.ratio` in the Go worker is already defined as (extracted-kept)/extracted and M8's production verification is written up in those terms ("47% dedup"). A panel whose "dedup ratio" meant the complement of the metric called dedup ratio is exactly the disagreement CONTEXT.md §7 warns about, and it would surface at the worst moment.

Frame-weighted, not chunk-weighted: this is a rate-of-sums over the raw counters, so a 600-frame chunk moves it proportionally more than a 3-frame one, which matches what actually drives R2 storage and labelling cost. The histogram's own mean (sum(rate(frames_dedup_ratio_sum))/sum(rate(frames_dedup_ratio_count))) weights every chunk equally regardless of size — the wrong denominator for a cost question, but still queryable directly if a per-chunk view is ever wanted.

Expect roughly 40-70% dropped (CONTEXT.md §4's design estimate; M8 measured 47% on real footage). A bad value is near 0% for a sustained period — the threshold (CROWDMON_DEDUP_THRESHOLD) is too tight and nothing is being deduplicated — or near 100%, where it is so loose that almost every frame is being discarded.

panels.title: Reclaim rate
panels.description: Rate of job.reclaimed spans — leases the Workers Cron reaper found stale and handed back to `pending` with attempts still remaining (CONTEXT.md §Q14/M6 amendment). Built from Tempo span metrics (traces_spanmetrics_calls_total), not a Worker counter, because @microlabs/otel-cf-workers exports traces only; this is the reason the reaper emits one span per reclaimed job instead of one span per tick with a count, since only span *rate* becomes a Prometheus series here. A reclaim at low attempts is an ordinary crash or a transient network error the worker didn't recover from; a bad value is a sustained non-zero rate, which means jobs are dying mid-run repeatedly — check whether it is one poison video climbing toward MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) or many different jobs, which point at different causes (a bad video vs. a bad box).

panels.title: Failure rate
panels.description: Rate of job.failed and job.retired spans combined — every way a job in this system permanently stops being retried. job.retired (CONTEXT.md §Q14/M6 amendment) is a reaper retirement: a lease that went stale with no attempts left. job.failed (M9.1) is the other half: a worker itself reporting a terminal failure on the first attempt — deleted, private, geo-blocked, members-only or age-gated video, the taxonomy in CONTEXT.md's M7 amendment to §Q13 — via POST /api/jobs/:id/complete, which now opens a span at the point it writes status='failed' to D1 (apps/api/src/routes/jobs.ts's recordJobFailed). Before M9.1 closed it this panel counted job.retired alone, and a reported failure — the more common path, since the reaper's ceiling exists for crashes rather than for reports the M6 amendment already separates out — was invisible here entirely; that gap is closed, not merely narrowed. A bad value is any sustained non-zero rate — every span counted here is a video permanently lost from the dataset. To tell a crash-driven retirement apart from a reported one, filter by span_name in Tempo directly; this panel intentionally shows their sum, not their split.

panels.title: Pre-label duration
panels.description: p50 and p95 wall time for a whole `prelabel` job — sample selection, one `image.detect` call per sampled frame, and the prediction write (M11.4, CONTEXT.md §9.3's promotion trigger made concrete). Same shape as Download duration beside it, and for the same reason: nothing about M11 asked for an image or box count as a Prometheus series the way M8.2 asked for frames extracted/kept — those numbers already live as attributes on `job.prelabel` and its children (`crowdmon.prelabel.sampled`, `crowdmon.prelabel.boxes`, `crowdmon.prelabel.boxes_by_class`), so a duration histogram alongside them would be a second source for a number `job.prelabel`'s own span already carries, with nothing to disagree about only because it would be measuring the same span metrics-generator already turns into `traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket`. A bad value is p95 pulling away from p50 — the detector sidecar sharing the box's two cores with a live chunk job (`worker/internal/detect/client.go`'s comment on the CPU budget), or `CROWDMON_PRELABEL_SAMPLE_SIZE` having grown past the 200-image default (`worker/internal/sample/sample.go`).

panels.title: Pre-label throughput
panels.description: Images per second the detector actually finished, as the call rate of `image.detect` — one span per sampled frame (M11.4), read the same way Reclaim rate reads `job.reclaimed`: span *rate* is the only shape a one-span-per-unit-of-work signal turns into in Prometheus, and the alternative (a counter incremented next to the span) would be the same redundant-second-source the Pre-label duration panel's description argues against. This is the number CONTEXT.md §12's CPU sizing claim is about — an i5-7200U running open-vocabulary detection in low seconds per image on two cores with no GPU. A bad value is this dropping toward zero while Queue depth's `prelabel`/`pending` series climbs: the sidecar is up but starved, most likely sharing its two cores with a live chunk job (the same contention Chunk duration's own description names).

panels.title: Pre-label failure rate
panels.description: Rate of `job.prelabel` spans that ended in error — the sidecar down, an image object missing from R2, a rejected prediction report (`worker/internal/worker/pipeline.go`'s `prelabel` branch is the full classification). Read off `job.prelabel`'s own span status (`status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"`) rather than folded into the Failure rate panel above: `job.failed` and `job.retired` are API-side spans, and Tempo's spanmetrics connector on this box only promotes `service`, `span_name` and `status_code` as dimensions — no job-kind label to filter Failure rate down to prelabel specifically (checked live against the collector; `traces_spanmetrics_calls_total`'s label set has no third dimension to split on). `job.prelabel` already carries the kind in its own span name, so its status code is this signal's whole source rather than something added for this panel. A bad value is any sustained non-zero rate here, distinct from Failure rate's crash-or-report mix: a prelabel job retries up to the same attempt ceiling (CONTEXT.md §Q14) before the video's frames simply never get boxes, which is not a job.failed/job.retired event on the API side today — it is silence, a video that stays out of the pool M11's own done-when clause promises it would enter.
